lead.headline: Storj Bankruptcy Tests Whether Tokenholders Get Anything in Chapter 11
lead.tldr: A decentralized infrastructure pioneer is attempting to convert token rights into bankruptcy equity, while institutional crypto rails advance elsewhere. The divergence between protocol-level distress and TradFi adoption is sharpening.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the infrastructure layer shows its fragility while institutional plumbing keeps getting laid, and the gap between those two stories is where we think the next repricing starts.

top_signals.title: Storj files for bankruptcy, explores equity path for tokenholders 20m, Storj files for bankruptcy, explores equity path for tokenholders The decentralized storage provider says its network will continue operating during Chapter 11 as it explores a court-approved ownership mechanism for STORJ holders.
top_signals.summary: Decentralized storage provider Storj has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The company intends to keep its network operational while exploring a court-approved mechanism to provide equity to STORJ token holders.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Storj's Chapter 11 filing with a proposed equity conversion for tokenholders establishes a precedent that decentralized networks can enter traditional bankruptcy proceedings without immediate network shutdown, but the recovery value for STORJ holders will depend on whether a court recognizes token claims as equity-like and how the estate values a still-operating decentralized network.

top_signals.title: Russia’s Sberbank to launch crypto trading infrastructure this year10m, Russia’s Sberbank to launch crypto trading infrastructure this yearRussia’s biggest bank plans to create cryptocurrency trading infrastructure by Dec. 1 as the country is set to establish rules for market participants while allowing crypto assets to be used in foreign trade operations.
top_signals.summary: Russia's largest bank, Sberbank, intends to launch a cryptocurrency trading infrastructure by December 1. This move aligns with new national rules allowing the use of crypto assets for foreign trade operations.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Sberbank's December 1 deadline for crypto trading infrastructure creates a controlled experiment in state-sanctioned institutional crypto rails under sanctions pressure, where the bank's foreign trade use case may generate transaction volume that Western exchanges and infrastructure providers cannot legally access.

top_signals.title: KB Kookmin Bank to Launch JPMorgan Kinexys Cross-Border Payment Service
top_signals.summary: KB Kookmin Bank is integrating JPMorgan's Kinexys blockchain platform to facilitate cross-border US dollar settlements. The service will operate across 10 different countries, marking a significant institutional adoption of blockchain for traditional banking payments.
top_signals.why_it_matters: KB Kookmin's Kinexys integration across ten countries demonstrates that JPMorgan's blockchain settlement layer has achieved product-market fit with Asian commercial banks seeking dollar alternatives, and this deployment pattern likely accelerates competitive responses from other correspondent banking relationships.

top_signals.title: BitMart to Wind Down Exchange as BMX Tanks
top_signals.summary: BitMart has announced it will wind down its cryptocurrency exchange operations following reports of user withdrawal delays. Trading is set to halt on August 26, with all platform operations ceasing in January.
top_signals.why_it_matters: BitMart's wind-down following withdrawal delays and BMX token collapse continues the exchange consolidation pattern where secondary platforms without differentiated liquidity or regulatory positioning face accelerated failure, concentrating volume and counterparty risk among fewer venues.

top_signals.title: CFTC issues second warning to prediction markets on cookie-cutter self-certifications36m, CFTC issues second warning to prediction markets on cookie-cutter self-certificationsFor the second time this year, the regulator told prediction markets to stop issuing overly broad, template-style certifications of events contracts.
top_signals.summary: The CFTC has issued its second warning of the year to prediction markets regarding the use of template-style self-certifications for event contracts. The regulator is demanding more specific and rigorous certifications to ensure compliance with trading regulations.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The CFTC's second warning on prediction market self-certifications signals escalating enforcement intent against event contract platforms that relied on template compliance, and this regulatory tightening will likely raise capital requirements and legal costs for prediction market operators seeking US market access.

on_the_radar.title: Robinhood in talks to add Crypto.com prediction markets as Kalshi rivalry grows: WSJ
on_the_radar.summary: Robinhood is reportedly in discussions to integrate Crypto.com's prediction markets, allowing users to trade yes-or-no contracts. This move is seen as a strategic effort to compete with the growing influence of Kalshi.

on_the_radar.title: Investors use crypto exchanges to avoid Beijing’s controls on AI stocks
on_the_radar.summary: Investors are utilizing crypto exchanges and perpetual futures to bypass Chinese government restrictions on foreign access to AI-related stocks. This trend highlights the use of digital asset platforms as a workaround for traditional equity market controls.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin’s Largest Institutions Launch $15m Security Initiative
on_the_radar.summary: Major Bitcoin institutions have launched a $15 million initiative aimed at improving the network's security. The move addresses the concept of Bitcoin's security as a public good that requires dedicated funding to sustain.

on_the_radar.title: Brazil puts tokenized cows to work as loan collateral: Report25m, Brazil puts tokenized cows to work as loan collateral: ReportTen tokenized dairy cows backed a $19,600 loan registered on Brazil’s B3, in one of Brazil’s first uses of tokenized livestock as loan collateral.
on_the_radar.summary: Brazil has implemented one of its first uses of tokenized livestock as loan collateral. Ten tokenized dairy cows were used to back a $19,600 loan registered on the B3 exchange.

on_the_radar.title: Former bitcoin miner Poolin files Chapter 11, sets $52 million floor bid for Texas operations
on_the_radar.summary: Former Bitcoin miner Poolin Technology has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection with $173 million in claims. The company has established a $52 million floor bid for the sale of its mining operations located in Texas.

worth_a_read.title: Formally Verifying a Compiler Using Automated Research
worth_a_read.note: Paradigm's work on formally verifying compilers with automated research tools is worth tracking because compiler correctness underpins the security of any smart contract execution environment, and formal methods are moving from academic exercise to deployable infrastructure.

worth_a_read.title: CLARITY’s Combined Text Is Here. Now It Needs Votes
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of the CLARITY Act's combined text provides the most current legislative text for understanding how the bill's provisions on stablecoin and market structure will actually function if brought to a vote, which remains uncertain.

worth_a_read.title: Bitcoin’s Largest Institutions Launch $15m Security Initiative
worth_a_read.note: The $15 million Bitcoin security initiative led by institutional holders including MicroStrategy and Marathon Digital represents a material commitment to network security that shifts some defensive burden from miners to large holders with concentrated exposure.

linkedin_post:
Storj filed Chapter 11 today and wants to give tokenholders equity. That's not a pivot. That's a last-resort conversion of a token structure that didn't produce sustainable cash flows into whatever a bankruptcy court will recognize. The network keeps running, which is technically interesting—decentralized infrastructure doesn't need the corporate entity to function. But the economic question is what STORJ holders actually recover, and whether any future equity carries value without the token incentive mechanism that built the supply side in the first place.

We're watching this because it tests a thesis we underwrote poorly in 2017: that protocol tokens and equity would converge. They haven't. Storj is trying to force convergence in a Delaware courtroom.

Meanwhile KB Kookmin is live on JPMorgan's Kinexys across ten countries. Sberbank builds its own rails by December. The institutions aren't waiting for token governance to resolve itself. They're building on permissioned infrastructure with known counterparties and regulatory cover.

The repricing we underwrite on is between those two worlds. Not whether decentralized storage works—Storj proved it works—but whether the token model funds it, and whether the institutions building parallel rails capture the value that tokens couldn't monetize.

Our test: if Storj's equity conversion gets court approval and the network still loses storage providers, the token-to-equity bridge collapses. If providers stay without token incentives, the entire decentralized storage sector gets repriced.
